I did not re-fetch them, so treat them as source claims, not measurements.

Defect → code: (3) slab skyline = ridge() ring at scenery:583-598 (flat boxes, hMin 18-54 m, no taper). (5) cork oak = scenery:17-54 (crown frusta 0.72·h wide, bark strip 26 % of h) is out-scaled by stone pine (def l.83) and forestEdge pines at 0.78 share. (2) night glow has no code cause in the circuit files: def has no lamps; the source must be shared lighting/headlamp code (not traced). (1) and (4) are in the shared lighting path (js/lighting/atmosphere.js wet/rain branches near l.357-393 and haze), not in either circuit file.

Ranked defects & suggested fixes (not applied)

  1. Wet / rain / storm ground loses all colour and mirrors props. Frames #7–18, 31–36, 43–48. Grass and red earth collapse to grey; trees and stands cast dark vertical reflection streaks and the cork-oak crowns turn pale-translucent. Mechanism lives in the wet-surface / planar reflection response (js/lighting/atmosphere.js wet blend, backend wet path), not in scenery/portimao.js; likely the wetness term is applied to terrain albedo and specular too strongly. Fix: cap terrain wetness darkening and reflection strength (renderer/lighting owner). Confidence: seen on all 3 wet weathers.
  2. Night without lamps still reads as floodlit. #49–60. night:false and furniture.lamp:"none" (portimao.js:~58) yet red-earth runoff glows warm in broad pools and the sky is pure black. Either add real mast lamps or lower the unexplained fill; decision for the parent. Source of the glow not identified (car lights vs. ambient) — uncertain.
  3. Skyline is a flat-topped slab wall. Visible in nearly every day frame at the horizon (e.g. #4, #5): the "Monchique foothills" ring is straight-edged box slabs, at odds with the brief's rolling hills. Fix: shape the far terrain/ridge profile in scenery/portimao.js ridge() calls (~l.593) with varied height and slope, or lower terrainOuter (125) flat rim.
  4. Dusk haze overwhelms the scene. #41 (f67 dusk dry) is a solid yellow wash that hides the hamlet and the stand. Fog/horizon colour at dusk too strong against pal.fogColor [.78 .74 .64].
  5. Cork oak and stone pine are hard to tell apart. The brief wants a low, wide red-trunk cork oak; the frames mostly show umbrella shapes on thin trunks plus conifer-like pines, so the montado idea hardly reads at orbit distance (scenery:17–54 sizes: crown 0.72·h wide, h 7.5–10.5 m).
  6. Minor: trackside camera at f00 is swallowed by a paddock block (#67) — probably the shot tool's placement (uncertain). Mid-sector (#4, #28) left side looks bare red earth where hillsideTerrace(0.470,0.500,−1) should show terracing — unconfirmed which side the orbit view shows.

Not captured / uncertain

  • Elevation vs real circuit not compared to survey data; built length −0.6 % is vs. the source claim of 4653 m, not an independent measurement.

  • Filename note: shots use the gallery parser's <view>-<tod>-<condition> order (docs/tracks/GALLERY.md), not the brief's weather-then-tod. storm is not in the parser's WEATHER_TAIL so storm frames group under a "view-day" sector.
